chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd Al-Yaqtini. And I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd Al-Yaqtini.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَىٰ: Muhammad ibn Isa, a key narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنِ عِيسَىٰ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ الْ: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd Al-Yaqtini, the source narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the narration chain for Muhammad ibn Isa verified in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage serves as a critical validation of the *Thiqa* (reliable) status of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd Al-Yaqtini, a key narrator in the Kufan school, by demonstrating his transmission through two independent, high-authority chains: one via Shaykh al-Saduq’s father and the other via the prominent scholar Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar. By explicitly linking these paths, al-Saduq reinforces the authenticity of the hadiths attributed to him, addressing potential scholarly scrutiny regarding the reliability of the Kufan narrators during the period of *Tadlis* (concealment of details).
